- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to account for bullish momentum.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model often over-optimistically peaks; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high or use moving average of last 5 days.
- After a sharp spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply a 1–3 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model tends to hold too high; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.33, 1.00, 0.33), model may misread trend direction; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 10-day average to reduce lag bias.
